mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the demand signal, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within 2 months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face higher costs.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in 3 months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the supply signal, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the demand signal, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as liquidity is abundant.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances with FEDFUNDS < 1%, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% within the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the labor market signal, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter, it signals inflationary pressures alongside strong economic growth, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% month-over-month and GDPC1 increase > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the demand signal, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
